subject: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Cho <anna@omnitech.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist

Team —

Quick kickoff note as we lock the OKR slate for the quarter and prepare the QBR packet for OmniTech. High level asks below; I want alignment on scope boundaries (what we commit to measure vs. aspirational goals) and a concise readiness checklist for the executive readout.

Top items for this thread:
- Confirm final objective wording and one-line success criteria by EOD.
- Agree canonical measurement sources and owners (for any metric we present).
- Validate the QBR slide checklist (who presents which metric, and fallback narrators).
- Attachments: initial checklist and a sample measurement export attached.

I'm proposing we keep the slate tight — 3 primary objectives for the customer-facing workstream, with clear guardrails for cadence and latency SLO reporting.

Please reply with owners and any blockers. I attached the draft checklist (QBR_readiness_checklist.xlsx) — Marissa, can you take the lead on narrative and presenter assignment? Neha, can you validate the measurement exports and flag any gaps?

Thanks,
Lukas
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_readiness_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist

Thanks — quick responses inline.

- I can own narrative + presenter assignment. Proposed split: Marissa (customer health + adoption), Vivek (performance/cost), Lukas (roadmap/ask). Kimberly to manage the stakeholder slide + legal/contract highlights.
- For objectives: I suggest we tighten Objective 2 to read: "Reduce inference unit cost by 18% for production text-generation workloads (p95 latency <= 120ms)." That keeps cost + latency in the same success criteria.
- On measurement sources: Neha — we need a canonical definition for "inference unit" and a consistent tokenization approach. If we can't confidently produce aligned numbers, call it out in the notes rather than risk a mismatch in QBR.

I also added two rows to the checklist (column for presenter and backup) and highlighted open items in yellow. See attached snapshot in the doc link below.

Marissa
Sr. Director, Growth
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist

Hi Lukas & team —

Thanks for the head's up, and glad to see the checklist. A couple of items from our side before the QBR:
- For the cost reduction objective, can you break down the expected impact by feature area (streaming, batching, caching)? Our finance team will want that granularity.
- On the latency SLA, are you planning to show regional splits? We operate in both US and EU regions and will need per-region p95 numbers.
- Please include the short list of mitigations you will trigger if measurements regress during the quarter.

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute pre-QBR dry run with our CS leadership on Tue morning.

Anna
Director, Customer Success
OmniTech
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Anna Cho <anna@omnitech.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 13:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist

Looping in the measurement export — attached OKR_measurements_v1.csv (sample). Notes:
- Canonical inference unit defined as: generated token count as recorded by the serving runtime, per-request; tokenization uses GPT-style byte-pair approach for parity with prior quarters.
- Regional splits included (us, eu). The sample shows current baseline and projected uplift if we enable the new batching profile.
- Open data gaps: fallback logs from legacy instances are incomplete for March; I've flagged those rows in the CSV.

Action items from my side:
1) Clean up the legacy rows and produce final numbers by Mon EOD.
2) Add a short methodological note for the QBR appendix describing tokenization and rounding.

Neha
Lead, Data & Measurement
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OKR_measurements_v1.csv (CSV stub)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Anna Cho <anna@omnitech.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Quarterly kickstart: OKR boundaries, measurement SLAs, and QBR readiness checklist

Perfect — thanks everyone. Quick decisions:
- Objective wording finalized as Marissa suggested.
- Neha to publish cleaned numbers by Mon EOD and drop the appendix methodological note in the shared doc.
- Marissa will own the presenter roster; Vivek to prepare the performance/cost breakout by feature area (streaming/batching/caching) with EU/US splits.
- Kimberly, please confirm legal remarks to include on the stakeholder slide (any contract caveats, billing thresholds).
- Lukas will run the pre-QBR dry run with Anna and OmniTech on Tue 10:00am PT (Anna — please confirm if that works).

If there are no objections, I'll mark this thread as the canonical decisions log for the quarter's customer-facing OKRs.

Thanks — let's close any remaining open checklist items by Monday so we have time for the dry run.

Lukas
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
